title: Deadline Ransom
subtitle: Ransomware on the NAS and the processing workstation before a client deadline

brief.userPrompt: Ten days before CP&L Deliverable D-3 is due, the processing team arrives on a weekday morning to find HUOG-NAS01 and the processing workstation HUOG-PROC01 encrypted with a ransom note on the share; the NAS snapshot schedule was disabled two nights earlier, GCS-02 was infected after it mounted the NAS to upload last week's flight logs, and the offline backup drive OB-1 in the General Manager's safe is three weeks old. The Group must isolate the Data VLAN at HUOG-FW01, keep the GCS fleet off the network and decide whether flights can continue, scope whether CP&L and CVAC client data was read and not only encrypted, recover from OB-1 and the off-site service in the HUOG-ISP Section 9.3 order once the managed SOC confirms the environment is clean, decide within four hours whether to notify the clients that D-3 is at risk, and record the decision not to pay.
constraints: Every email address of the Group and its units uses the exercise domain huog.example; outside parties use fictional domains and fictional outlet names (Channel 10, the Harwick Daily News); never a real agency, company or newspaper domain.

Player roles are only those in the audience list; outside parties (clients, the managed SOC, Data Center Operations, the off-site backup service, the FBI, the media) are played by the SimCell, not seated as players.

overview.theme: Ransomware against a small operator’s mission data: grounding what touched it, scoping what was read, recovering in order from stale backups, and telling clients the truth inside their contract clocks
overview.threat: On Monday morning, October 5 — ten days before Calder Power & Light Deliverable D-3 is due — the processing team finds HUOG-NAS01 and the processing workstation HUOG-PROC01 encrypted, with a ransom note on the shares. The NAS snapshot schedule was disabled on Saturday night by the backup service account, the off-site backup job has been failing since a credential expired, and the offline drive OB-1 in the General Manager’s safe was last written three weeks ago. GCS-02 mounted the NAS at 08:44 to upload last week’s flight logs and is now infected too. Overnight on Sunday the same account read the controlled share, which holds CP&L task-order data and the PL-02 calibration files.
overview.operationalImpact: Processing for D-3 stops. The Data VLAN has to be isolated at HUOG-FW01 and every ground control station that mounted the NAS since Saturday grounded until the managed SOC (SecureWatch MSSP) clears it, which also threatens the CVAC growing-season collections due within seven days. The General Manager must decide within four hours whether to tell CP&L and CVAC that deadlines are at risk, and whether CP&L’s 24-hour exposure notice applies because its data may have been read and not only encrypted. Recovery follows HUOG-ISP Section 9.3: OB-1 is not connected until the MSSP confirms a clean environment, the calibration share comes back first and is verified against the repository hashes, and the last three September collection days for D-3 may survive only on the aircraft payload media. The Group does not pay, and records that decision.

overview.targetAudience: Leadership, Systems / Cybersecurity, Flight Operations, Payload & Calibration, Corporate Communications
overview.location: Millbrook Road hangar complex (Hangars 1–3), Harwick, Calder County, New York

objectives.name: Data Integrity Verification
objectives.text: Keep Leadership, the Systems & Cybersecurity Lead, Flight Operations, Payload & Calibration and Corporate Communications on one set of facts, and route every external statement through Corporate Communications (UC-CP-2025).

objectives.name: Client Notification Authority
objectives.text: Within four hours of discovery, decide whether to notify CP&L and CVAC that deadlines are at risk and whether CP&L’s 24-hour exposure notice applies, on the evidence available (HUOG-ISP 9.3 step 4), and record the decision not to pay.

objectives.name: Operational Continuity vs. System Containment
objectives.text: Contain the ransomware (isolate the Data VLAN at HUOG-FW01, ground every GCS that mounted the NAS during the infection window), scope which shares were read, and preserve evidence for the MSSP.

objectives.name: Incident Command Authority
objectives.text: Recover in the HUOG-ISP 9.3 order from OB-1 and the off-site service once the MSSP confirms a clean environment, verifying restored data against manifests before any processing.

roles.name: Director of Flight Operations (Flight Operations)
roles.description: Owns the flight schedule, crew rosters and the fleet register; decides which flights go and on which GCS.
standingOrders: No flight on a GCS that has not been cleared against the 03.2026-B baseline.
Crews do not connect a GCS to the NAS or accept updates until the Systems & Cybersecurity Lead says so.
Tell clients about flight changes through the Campaign Lead, with facts.
Keep the incident log in the incident folder on paper until the NAS is back.

roles.name: Systems & Cybersecurity Lead (Systems / Cybersecurity)
roles.description: Owns the GCS baseline, the networks, HUOG-FW01, the NAS and backups; incident lead for cyber events and liaison to the managed SOC.
standingOrders: Isolate the Data VLAN at HUOG-FW01 and disconnect the NAS; power down processing workstations only on the MSSP’s instruction.
A GCS that mounted the NAS during the infection window is infected and grounded.
OB-x is not connected until the MSSP confirms the environment is clean.
Restore in order: calibration share, ops records, the campaign with the nearest deadline, the rest; verify against manifests first.

roles.name: General Manager (Leadership)
roles.description: Accountable executive; decides on client and regulator notification, records the decision not to pay, and is the spokesperson with Corporate Communications.
standingOrders: Decide within four hours whether client deadlines are at risk and tell the clients the facts (HUOG-ISP 9.3).
CP&L’s 24-hour exposure notice applies if its data may have been read, not only encrypted.
The Group does not pay a ransom; record the decision and the reasons.
Nothing goes to the media except through Corporate Communications.

roles.name: Corporate Communications (Communications)
roles.description: Owns all external messaging under crisis protocol UC-CP-2025, including the media and social media; the Group never speaks to the media directly.
standingOrders: All media contact goes through Corporate Communications; staff do not comment.
Do not confirm a ransom, a demand or what was taken before the General Manager approves.
Clients hear from the Group before they read about it.
Give a time for the next update every time.

roles.name: Payload & Calibration Lead (Payload & Calibration)
roles.description: Owns payload integration, calibration data integrity, ground-truth records, processing for client deliverables and PL-02 export-control handling.
standingOrders: No restored data is processed until it matches its manifest.
The calibration share is verified against the repository hashes before anything else is restored.
Payload storage media are removable media: custody, no connection to an infected host.
Tell the General Manager a week ahead of any risk to a client date.

phases.title: Encrypted Shares
phases.goal: Recognize ransomware on the mission data, contain it and ground what touched it before more of the fleet is lost.
beats: At 09:05 the processing team finds the D-3 folders renamed and a ransom note on the share; HUOG-PROC01 shows the same note.
At 09:07 a local post shows the Group’s drones sitting on the pad on a flying day.
At 09:12 the NAS log shows the snapshot schedule disabled on Saturday and GCS-02 mounting the NAS at 08:44.
At 09:25 GCS-02 in Hangar 2 shows the ransom wallpaper; at 09:30 the backup alert shows OB-1 three weeks old and the off-site job failing.

phases.title: Scope
phases.goal: Find out what was encrypted, what was read and what can still fly, while the first client and the press call.
beats: At 10:05 CP&L calls about D-3; at 10:08 the MSSP flags a script on HUOG-PROC01 that turns out to be the processing team’s own.
At 10:15 the flight board shows today’s CVAC collection depending on GCS that may have touched the NAS.
At 10:25 the NAS audit shows the controlled share read on Sunday night and data leaving through HUOG-FW01.
At 10:30 the MSSP’s first assessment arrives.

phases.title: The Four-Hour Call
phases.goal: Decide what to tell CP&L and CVAC inside the four-hour window, with the backups stale and the scope still uncertain.
beats: At 11:05 a clean-laptop hash check shows OB-1 holds six of the nine D-3 collection days.
At 11:15 the Compliance Officer sets out the clocks: this is the decision point.
At 11:20 the UAS-11 payload SSDs may hold the missing days; at 11:30 the MSSP clears two GCS and grounds another.

phases.title: Recover in Order
phases.goal: Restore in the right order, verify before processing, keep the fleet flying for the next deadline and record the decision not to pay.
beats: At 12:05 the calibration share is restored from OB-1 and verified; at 12:10 the Harwick Daily News asks whether the Group paid.
At 12:15 CVAC asks about its farm data; at 12:20 the missing D-3 days are found on the payload media.
At 12:30 Flight Operations needs crews and clean GCS for tomorrow’s CVAC flights; at 12:55 counsel asks for the decision not to pay in writing.

msel.event: STARTEX: It is 09:00 on Monday, October 5. CP&L Deliverable D-3 — calibrated hyperspectral cubes from the Lakeshore summer campaign — is due on October 15. The processing team is in Hangar 3; two crews are preparing a CVAC field collection for 10:30. The weather is clear, 52°F. All systems were normal when the last person left on Friday.
msel.expectedAction: Each team states what it is working on today and what depends on the NAS.

msel.event: Email Forward: The processing analyst on HUOG-PROC01 reports that every file under \\HUOG-NAS01\campaigns\cpl-d3\ has been renamed with a .lck0 extension, a file README-RECOVER.txt sits in every folder, and HUOG-PROC01 shows the same note as its desktop background. The processing script fails its manifest check.
msel.expectedAction: The Payload & Calibration Lead stops all processing and tells the Systems & Cybersecurity Lead by phone; the Systems & Cybersecurity Lead starts HUOG-ISP 9.3: isolate the Data VLAN at HUOG-FW01, disconnect the NAS, leave HUOG-PROC01 powered on for the MSSP and call SecureWatch.

metrics.fail: A GCS that mounted the NAS kept flying, a host was reimaged or powered off without the MSSP, or OB-1 was connected before the clean confirmation.

metrics.name: Client Notification Decision
metrics.fail: No decision on CP&L within the four-hour window, or CP&L learned of the possible exposure from someone else; the decision not to pay was not recorded.
metrics.pass: At I-11 the General Manager decided what CP&L and CVAC were told and when, on the evidence of I-08, with the basis recorded; the no-pay decision was written down at I-18.
metrics.excellence: The notice included the realistic delivery date from I-15b, the publication threat from I-18 and a next-update time, and the PL-02 question went to the Compliance Officer.

metrics.name: Recovery in Order
metrics.fail: Data was processed before it was verified, the payload SSDs were copied onto an infected host, or the restore skipped the calibration share.
metrics.pass: The restore followed HUOG-ISP 9.3 (I-14a); the SSDs stayed in custody (I-11b) and were read on the clean laptop (I-15b).
metrics.excellence: The team identified the payload media as the source of the missing days at I-10a and rebuilt their calibration from the paper sheets without delaying the rest.

metrics.excellence: Clients heard from the Group before the press reported, and every answer carried a next-update time.

objectiveCapabilities.why: The objective requires keeping leadership, technical, and communications teams aligned on facts and routing all external statements through Corporate Communications, which is a core function of operational coordination under HSEEP.

The objective mandates that all external messaging be coordinated and controlled through Corporate Communications, ensuring consistent, reliable, and actionable information is delivered to the public and stakeholders, which aligns with public information and warning.

The objective requires the General Manager to make a timely, fact-based decision on client notification within four hours, involving the Systems & Cybersecurity Lead and Compliance Officer, which depends on coordinated information flow across roles.

The decision to notify CP&L and CVAC depends on forensic evidence from the ransomware incident, including whether data was read or copied, which is a core function of cybersecurity in incident response and recovery.

The objective requires isolating the Data VLAN, grounding infected GCS units, and preserving evidence for forensic analysis — all actions defined in the HUOG-ISP 9.3 ransomware response procedure, which is a cybersecurity capability.

The objective involves stabilizing critical data systems (NAS, processing workstations) and restoring them in a defined order, which is a core function of infrastructure systems in response and recovery.

The objective requires the Incident Commander to lead recovery in a prescribed order, verify restored data against manifests, and ensure all actions follow the HUOG-ISP 9.3 recovery sequence, which is a function of operational coordination.
The objective involves restoring from verified backups, verifying data integrity, and ensuring no further compromise — all elements of cybersecurity in recovery and restoration.

modules.narrativeMd: It is 10:00. The Data VLAN has been isolated at HUOG-FW01, and the NAS is disconnected from the network. GCS-02 is grounded in Hangar 2. The processing team reports that all files under \HUOG-NAS01\campaigns\cpl-d3\ have been renamed with a .lck0 extension, and a ransom note is visible on HUOG-PROC01 and GCS-02. The HUOG-NAS01 log confirms that the snapshot schedule was disabled on Saturday at 22:15, and mass file renames began at 08:41 today from HUOG-PROC01 and GCS-02, which mounted the NAS at 08:44.
